title: Rockchip RK3668 switches to Cortex-A725 and Cortex-A520 cores, engineering samples planned for Q1 2027
summary:
More details have surfaced about the Rockchip RK3668 processor. The biggest change is that the Armv9 SoC will feature eight cores (6x Cortex-A725 and 2x Cortex-A520), rather than ten cores in a 4x Cortex-A730 + 6x Cortex-A530 configuration announced at its initial unveiling in July 2025. title: $69 Home Assistant Connect AUX-2 controller offers PoE, audio streaming, RS-232 control, Bluetooth proxy, and more
summary:
Nabu Casa has launched the Home Assistant Connect AUX-2, an ESP32-S3-based smart home controller that combines audio streaming, RS-232 serial control, Bluetooth LE proxy, and USB expansion for Z-Wave connectivity. It is designed for older audio systems, TVs, AV receivers, UPSs, solar inverters, and other devices to integrate into Home Assistant without cloud services. More specifically, the device features a Texas Instruments PCM5122 DAC for analog and optical audio output, two RS-232 ports, a USB-A port, and a Grove connector for additional sensors. It also supports 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi and Ethernet with 802.3af Power over Ethernet (PoE), so you can install it away from the main Home Assistant server. title: Home Assistant-compatible ESP32 4-channel PWM fan controller is designed for server racks and NAS systems
summary:
Designed by CoolMaker Lab in China, the ESP32 4-channel PWM fan controller is an open-source, Home Assistant-compatible board for managing cooling in server racks, NAS systems, network cabinets, and other DIY enclosures. It can independently control up to four 4-pin PWM fans, supporting PWM-based speed adjustment, tachometer-based RPM monitoring, and individual fan power switching. The controller supports up to four external DS18B20 temperature sensors for automatic fan speed adjustment, along with a web interface, an HTTP REST API, and Bluetooth proxy functionality. The latest v2.0 hardware and firmware also support optional LD2402G 24GHz mmWave radar for presence-based automation. It supports up to four simultaneous displays via HDMI 2.0 and USB4 ports, offers six USB Type-A ports, two 40 Gbps USB4 ports, and two 2.5 GbE ports, as well as Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 5.4 wireless connectivity. In this article, we will list the specifications, go through an unboxing and a teardown to check out the hardware, and boot the system to the pre-installed Windows 11 Pro operating system. A more detailed review with feature testing and benchmarks on both Windows 11 and Ubuntu 26.04 will be published in a few weeks.
